beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A correction can disappear into yesterday’s conversation, or improve tomorrow’s method.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Chapter Four explores the second possibility through reusable procedures.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The method preserves inputs, stages, and acceptance criteria while replacing old facts.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A layout mistake should not force someone to repeat valid research.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: But changing the objective may require new evidence, not a small repair.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The distinction is subtle, and the book gives it room to develop.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It connects corrections, dependencies, recovery, and evaluation into a picture of operational improvement.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: For readers building workflows, that development offers more than another prompting technique.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: AssistOS treats autonomy as specific permissions, rather than a single setting.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A worker may observe, propose changes, execute selected actions, or continue agreed work.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Those permissions can differ between development and production.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A document revision can be reversed more easily than a message already sent.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book uses such differences to examine where human authority should enter.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Supervision becomes a designed handoff, with useful freedom between meaningful checkpoints.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You gain a vocabulary for discussing delegation without treating autonomy as all-or-nothing.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The harder question is how those boundaries should work in your own organization.
